summary: This is Snowflake documentation for the ALTER PIPE SQL command, which modifies a limited set of properties of an existing pipe and performs operations such as pausing a pipe, refreshing it, and setting comments or tags. The note covers the syntax, parameters (including PIPE_EXECUTION_PAUSED, COMMENT, TAG, UNSET, REFRESH with PREFIX and MODIFIED_AFTER), usage notes on privileges and limitations, and examples. Navigation and boilerplate from the web page are ignored.
one_line: Snowflake reference for the ALTER PIPE command, covering pausing, refreshing, commenting and tagging Snowpipe pipes.
key_facts: ALTER PIPE modifies a limited set of properties for an existing pipe object and supports pausing a pipe, refreshing a pipe, adding/overwriting/removing a comment, and setting/unsetting a tag.
The PIPE_EXECUTION_PAUSED parameter accepts TRUE or FALSE and defaults to FALSE, meaning the pipe is running by default.
A pipe is considered stale when paused for longer than the limited retention period for event messages, which is 14 days by default.
Either a stale pipe or other specified scenarios require forcing the pipe to resume by calling the SYSTEM$PIPE_FORCE_RESUME function.
The tag value is always a string, and the maximum number of characters for a tag value is 256.
The REFRESH clause copies a set of staged data files to the Snowpipe ingest queue for loading into the target table, and can only load data files staged within the last 7 days.
The REFRESH PREFIX parameter path is appended to the stage reference in the pipe definition, and the path must be enclosed in single quotes.
The MODIFIED_AFTER parameter takes an ISO-8601 timestamp; its default and maximum allowed value is 7 days.
Only the pipe owner (the role with the OWNERSHIP privilege on the pipe) can set or unset properties on a pipe.
A non-owner role with the OPERATE privilege on the pipe can pause or resume it using SET PIPE_EXECUTION_PAUSED.
Non-owner roles refreshing a pipe need OPERATE on the pipe, USAGE on an external stage or READ on an internal stage in the pipe definition, and SELECT and INSERT on the target table.
It is not currently possible to modify the AWS_SNS_TOPIC or INTEGRATION parameters using ALTER PIPE.
The REFRESH functionality is intended for short term use to resolve specific issues when Snowpipe fails to load a subset of files and is not intended for regular use.
The example 'alter pipe mypipe SET PIPE_EXECUTION_PAUSED = true;' pauses the pipe named mypipe.
The example 'ALTER PIPE mypipe REFRESH PREFIX='d1/' MODIFIED_AFTER='2018-07-30T13:56:46-07:00';' loads only files under the d1 path staged after the given timestamp.
